position: Office of National Drug Control Policy
proposal: The Mandate says a political appointee should lead the ONDCP budget office, that the ONDCP Director should ensure in the immediate term that its grant programs fund the President's drug control priorities, and that ONDCP should be managed by committed political appointees. It names the Drug-Free Communities Support Program and then the High Intensity Drug Trafficking Areas Program and says it makes sense to transfer them eventually to the Department of Justice and the Department of Health and Human Services, respectively. Read in order, that pairs Drug-Free Communities with Justice and HIDTA with HHS; the text does not otherwise say which program goes where.

status_summary: The FY2026 and FY2027 ONDCP budget submissions both propose moving HIDTA to the Department of Justice and Drug-Free Communities to HHS, with zero dollars for each at ONDCP. For FY2027, the Justice Department's Office of Justice Programs budget requests 196 million dollars to take over HIDTA, and a coalition summary reports 70 million dollars for Drug-Free Communities in a proposed new HHS division; these sums are why the ONDCP submission shows zero. The FY2027 ONDCP submission lists FY2026 enacted levels of 298.6 million dollars for HIDTA and 109 million dollars for Drug-Free Communities at ONDCP, so no transfer has occurred. No information was found on who leads the ONDCP budget office.

timeline.event: ONDCP's FY2026 budget submission proposed transferring HIDTA to the Department of Justice and Drug-Free Communities to HHS, with zero dollars requested for each at ONDCP.
The Justice Department's FY2027 Office of Justice Programs budget submission requested 196 million dollars to fund HIDTA and transfer its management from ONDCP.

ONDCP's FY2027 budget submission again proposed moving HIDTA to Justice and Drug-Free Communities to HHS, with zero dollars at ONDCP, and listed FY2026 enacted levels of 298.6 and 109 million dollars.

title: Political appointee over ONDCP budget; steer grants; move DFC and HIDTA out of ONDCP
uncertainties: The ONDCP submissions carry no dates, so their dates are taken from the posting paths and, for FY2027, a coalition post of the same week; the Justice submission is dated March 2026 with the day approximate. The 70 million dollar Drug-Free Communities figure comes from a secondary source; the HHS budget document was not opened. The FY2026 enactment amounts are as stated in the FY2027 submission; the enacted appropriations law was not opened. The Mandate's literal pairing (Drug-Free Communities to Justice, HIDTA to HHS) is the reverse of the budget proposals; the record counts the proposals as aligned with the recommendation to move both programs out of ONDCP. The FY2027 request for ONDCP salaries and expenses was 21.8 million dollars and 72 positions. Who leads the ONDCP budget office was not found.
